Considering large language models (LLMs) have exhibited exceptional ability in language understanding, generation, interaction, and reasoning, we advocate that LLMs could act as a controller to manage existing AI models to solve complicated AI tasks and language could be a generic interface to empower t\\\",\\\\\\n    \\\"summary\\\": \\\"HuggingGPT is a framework using ChatGPT as a central controller to orchestrate various AI models from Hugging Face to solve complex tasks. yzhuang@zju.edu.cn Zhejiang University, Microsoft Research Asia Microsoft Research, Microsoft Research Asia Abstract Solving complicated AI tasks with different domains and modalities is a key step toward artificial general intelligence. While there are abundant AI models available for different domains and modalities, they cannot handle complicated AI tasks. Considering large language models (LLMs) have exhibited exceptional ability in language understanding, generation, interaction, and reasoning, we advocate that LLMs could act as a controller to manage existing AI models to solve complicated AI tasks and language could be a generic interface to empower t\\\",\\\\\\n    \\\"summary\\\": \\\"HuggingGPT is a framework using ChatGPT as a central controller to orchestrate various AI models from Hugging Face to solve complex tasks. ChatGPT plans the task, selects appropriate models based on their descriptions, executes subtasks, and summarizes the results. This approach addresses limitations of LLMs by allowing them to handle multimodal data (vision, speech) and coordinate multiple models for complex tasks, paving the way for more advanced AI systems.\\\",\\\\\\n    \\\"highlights\\\": [\\\\\\n      \\\"2) Recently, some researchers started to investigate the integration of using tools or models in LLMs  .\\\"\\\\\\n    ],\\\\\\n - 
```diff
+ # Exa API Integration Guide
+ 
+ This rule provides comprehensive guidance for integrating with the Exa API, a powerful search and retrieval service for finding, analyzing, and extracting information from web content. Exa offers semantic search, content retrieval, similarity finding, and question answering capabilities.
+ 
+ ## Core Methods Overview
+ 
+ Exa offers four primary methods that can be used individually or in combination for various search and retrieval needs:
+ 
+ 1. **Search**: Find relevant web content based on semantic or keyword queries
+ 2. **Find Similar**: Discover content similar to a reference URL
+ 3. **Contents Retrieval**: Extract and process content from web pages
+ 4. **Answer**: Generate direct answers to questions with citations
+ 
+ ## Installation and Setup
+ 
+ Install the official SDK for TypeScript/JavaScript applications:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ // Install via npm
+ npm install exa-js
+ 
+ // Initialize client
+ import Exa from 'exa-js';
+ const exa = new Exa(process.env.EXA_API_KEY);
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Search Method
+ 
+ The Search method finds relevant web content based on queries with optional content retrieval.
+ 
+ ### Basic Search
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ // Simple search returning just URLs and metadata
+ const result = await exa.search(
+   "latest advancements in quantum computing",
+   {
+     numResults: 10,
+     type: "auto" // Options: "auto", "neural", "keyword"
+   }
+ );
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Search with Content Retrieval
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ // Search with full text content
+ const resultWithText = await exa.searchAndContents(
+   "AI in healthcare",
+   {
+     text: true,
+     numResults: 5
+   }
+ );
+ 
+ // Search with highlights
+ const resultWithHighlights = await exa.searchAndContents(
+   "AI in healthcare",
+   {
+     highlights: true,
+     numResults: 5
+   }
+ );
+ 
+ // Search with both text and highlights
+ const resultWithTextAndHighlights = await exa.searchAndContents(
+   "AI in healthcare",
+   {
+     text: true,
+     highlights: true,
+     numResults: 5
+   }
+ );
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Search Parameters
+ 
+ | Parameter | Type | Description | Default |
+ |-----------|------|-------------|---------|
+ | query | string | The search query | Required |
+ | numResults | number | Number of results to return | 10 |
+ | type | string | Search type: "auto", "neural", "keyword" | "auto" |
+ | includeDomains | string[] | Limit results to specific domains | undefined |
+ | excludeDomains | string[] | Exclude specific domains | undefined |
+ | category | string | Specific category focus (e.g., "research paper", "news") | undefined |
+ | text | boolean or object | Return full text of results | undefined |
+ | highlights | boolean or object | Return relevant highlights from results | undefined |
+ | startPublishedDate | string | Only include results published after this date | undefined |
+ | endPublishedDate | string | Only include results published before this date | undefined |
+ 
+ ## Find Similar Method
+ 
+ The Find Similar method discovers web content similar to a reference URL.
+ 
+ ### Basic Usage
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ // Find pages similar to a reference URL
+ const similarResults = await exa.findSimilar(
+   "https://www.example.com/article-about-ai",
+   {
+     numResults: 5,
+     excludeSourceDomain: true
+   }
+ );
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Find Similar with Content
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ // Find similar with content retrieval
+ const similarWithContent = await exa.findSimilarAndContents(
+   "https://www.example.com/article",
+   {
+     text: true,
+     highlights: true,
+     numResults: 5
+   }
+ );
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Find Similar Parameters
+ 
+ | Parameter | Type | Description | Default |
+ |-----------|------|-------------|---------|
+ | url | string | Reference URL to find similar content | Required |
+ | numResults | number | Number of results to return | 10 |
+ | excludeSourceDomain | boolean | Exclude results from same domain as URL | false |
+ | includeDomains | string[] | Limit results to specific domains | undefined |
+ | excludeDomains | string[] | Exclude specific domains | undefined |
+ | text | boolean or object | Return full text of results | undefined |
+ | highlights | boolean or object | Return relevant highlights from results | undefined |
+ 
+ ## Contents Retrieval
+ 
+ The Contents method extracts and retrieves content from web pages by ID/URL.
+ 
+ ### Usage
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ // Get content for a single URL
+ const singleContent = await exa.getContents("https://www.example.com/article");
+ 
+ // Get content for multiple URLs
+ const multipleContents = await exa.getContents([
+   "https://www.example.com/article1",
+   "https://www.example.com/article2"
+ ]);
+ 
+ // Get content with specific options
+ const contentWithOptions = await exa.getContents(
+   ["https://www.example.com/article"],
+   {
+     text: { maxCharacters: 1000 },
+     highlights: { 
+       query: "artificial intelligence", 
+       numSentences: 2,
+       highlightsPerUrl: 3
+     }
+   }
+ );
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Content Types
+ 
+ 1. **Text**: Full text content of web pages
+ 2. **Highlights**: Key excerpts relevant to a query
+ 3. **Summary**: AI-generated summaries of page content
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ // Requesting structured summaries with a JSON schema
+ const contentsWithSchema = await exa.getContents(
+   "https://www.example.com/company-page",
+   {
+     summary: {
+       query: "Provide company information",
+       schema: {
+         "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
+         "title": "Company Information",
+         "type": "object",
+         "properties": {
+           "name": { "type": "string", "description": "The name of the company" },
+           "industry": { "type": "string", "description": "The industry the company operates in" },
+           "foundedYear": { "type": "number", "description": "The year the company was founded" }
+         },
+         "required": ["name", "industry"]
+       }
+     }
+   }
+ );
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Answer Method
+ 
+ The Answer method generates direct answers to questions using web content as a source.
+ 
+ ### Usage
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ // Basic question answering
+ const answer = await exa.answer(
+   "What is the latest valuation of SpaceX?",
+   {
+     text: true
+   }
+ );
+ 
+ // Using exa-pro model for improved results
+ const enhancedAnswer = await exa.answer(
+   "What are the most significant recent advances in CRISPR technology?",
+   {
+     model: "exa-pro",
+     text: true
+   }
+ );
+ 
+ // Stream response for progressive rendering
+ const streamingAnswer = await exa.answer(
+   "Explain the current state of quantum computing",
+   {
+     stream: true,
+     text: true
+   }
+ );
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Answer Parameters
+ 
+ | Parameter | Type | Description | Default |
+ |-----------|------|-------------|---------|
+ | query | string | The question to answer | Required |
+ | model | string | Model to use: "exa" or "exa-pro" | "exa" |
+ | stream | boolean | Return response as a stream | false |
+ | text | boolean | Include full text in citations | false |
+ 
+ ## Advanced Search Techniques
+ 
+ ### 1. Writing Continuation Queries
+ 
+ Use Exa to find content that logically continues a piece of writing:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ const currentText = &#96;The impact of climate change on global agriculture has been significant.
+ Rising temperatures and changing precipitation patterns have led to shifts
+ in crop yields and growing seasons. Some regions have experienced increased
+ drought stress, while&#96;;
+ 
+ const continuationQuery = currentText + " If you found the above interesting, here's another useful resource to read:";
+ const result = await exa.search(continuationQuery, { type: "neural" });
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### 2. Long Semantic Queries
+ 
+ Leverage Exa's capability to handle long, detailed queries:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ const longQuery = &#96;Abstract: In this study, we investigate the potential of quantum-enhanced 
+ machine learning algorithms for drug discovery applications. We present a novel 
+ quantum-classical hybrid approach that leverages quantum annealing for feature 
+ selection and a quantum-inspired tensor network for model training.&#96;;
+ 
+ const result = await exa.search(longQuery, { type: "neural" });
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### 3. Phrase-Filtered Search
+ 
+ Combine neural search with keyword filtering:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ const result = await exa.search(
+   "Companies developing sustainable materials", 
+   {
+     type: "neural",
+     includeText: ["biodegradable polymers"]
+   }
+ );
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Handling Search Results
+ 
+ Search results contain rich metadata and optional content that can be processed for various use cases:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ // Processing search results
+ const processResults = (results) =&gt; {
+   results.forEach(result =&gt; {
+     console.log(&#96;Title: ${result.title}&#96;);
+     console.log(&#96;URL: ${result.url}&#96;);
+     console.log(&#96;Published: ${result.publishedDate || 'Unknown'}&#96;);
+     console.log(&#96;Author: ${result.author || 'Unknown'}&#96;);
+     
+     if (result.text) {
+       console.log(&#96;Content length: ${result.text.length} chars&#96;);
+     }
+     
+     if (result.highlights &amp;&amp; result.highlights.length &gt; 0) {
+       console.log("Key highlights:");
+       result.highlights.forEach((highlight, i) =&gt; {
+         console.log(&#96;  ${i+1}. ${highlight}&#96;);
+       });
+     }
+     
+     console.log("---");
+   });
+ };
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Best Practices
+ 
+ 1. **Choose the right search type**:
+    - Use "neural" for conceptual, exploratory searches
+    - Use "keyword" for specific terms or proper nouns
+    - Use "auto" (default) when unsure
+ 
+ 2. **Craft effective queries**:
+    - For neural search, include context and be specific
+    - For finding similar content, choose representative URLs
+    - Consider using prompts like "Here is a link to..." for better results
+ 
+ 3. **Optimize content retrieval**:
+    - Request only the content types you need (text, highlights, summary)
+    - Use highlights for extracting relevant passages
+    - Set appropriate limits for maxCharacters and highlightsPerUrl
+ 
+ 4. **Handle rate limits and errors**:
+    - Implement exponential backoff for retries
+    - Monitor usage and costs with the costDollars response field
+    - Check error responses and handle appropriately
+ 
+ ## Error Handling Example
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ try {
+   const result = await exa.search("quantum computing advances");
+   // Process results
+ } catch (error) {
+   if (error.status === 429) {
+     console.error("Rate limit exceeded. Try again later.");
+   } else if (error.status === 401) {
+     console.error("Authentication error. Check your API key.");
+   } else {
+     console.error("Error performing search:", error.message);
+   }
+ }
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Performance Considerations
+ 
+ 1. **Request only what you need**:
+    - Limit numResults to reduce response time and costs
+    - Only request text, highlights, or summary when needed
+ 
+ 2. **Cache responses when appropriate**:
+    - Consider caching search results for frequently used queries
+    - Respect TTL and freshness requirements for your use case
+ 
+ 3. **Monitor costs**:
+    - The API returns costDollars information in responses
+    - Track usage to stay within budget
+ 
+ ## Example Integrations
+ 
+ ### RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ // Simple RAG implementation with Exa
+ async function generateWithRAG(userQuery) {
+   // Step 1: Retrieve relevant information
+   const searchResults = await exa.searchAndContents(
+     userQuery,
+     { highlights: true, numResults: 3 }
+   );
+   
+   // Step 2: Format context from search results
+   let context = "Here is some relevant information:\n\n";
+   searchResults.results.forEach((result, i) =&gt; {
+     context += &#96;[${i+1}] ${result.title}\n&#96;;
+     result.highlights.forEach(highlight =&gt; {
+       context += &#96;- ${highlight}\n&#96;;
+     });
+     context += &#96;Source: ${result.url}\n\n&#96;;
+   });
+   
+   // Step 3: Send to your LLM of choice with context and query
+   // const llmResponse = await yourLLM.complete({ 
+   //   prompt: &#96;${context}\n\nBased on the above information, ${userQuery}&#96; 
+   // });
+   
+   // Return response with citations
+   // return { 
+   //   answer: llmResponse.text,
+   //   sources: searchResults.results.map(r =&gt; r.url)
+   // };
+ }
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Response Schemas
+ 
+ ### Search Response
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ interface SearchResponse {
+   results: Result[];  // List of search results
+   autopromptString?: string;  // Generated autoprompt if used
+ }
+ 
+ interface Result {
+   url: string;  // URL of the result
+   id: string;   // Temporary ID for the document
+   title: string | null;  // Title of the result
+   score?: number;  // Relevance score (0-1)
+   publishedDate?: string;  // Estimated creation date
+   author?: string;  // Author if available
+ }
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Contents Response
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ interface ContentsResponse {
+   results: ContentResult[];  // List of content results
+ }
+ 
+ interface ContentResult extends Result {
+   text?: string;  // Full text if requested
+   highlights?: string[];  // Relevant excerpts if requested
+   highlightScores?: number[];  // Relevance scores for highlights
+   summary?: string;  // Summary if requested
+ }
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Answer Response
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;typescript
+ interface AnswerResponse {
+   answer: string;  // Generated answer text
+   citations: Citation[];  // Sources used for the answer
+ }
+ 
+ interface Citation {
+   id: string;  // Document ID
+   url: string;  // URL of the source
+   title: string;  // Title of the source
+   author?: string;  // Author if available
+   publishedDate?: string;  // Publication date if available
+   text?: string;  // Full text if requested
+ }
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
```
